title: Investigation 01: Microsoft Security Alert
subject: Two Microsoft Security Notifications
scenario:
EMAIL A
From: Microsoft 365 Security <no-reply@accountprotection.microsoft.com>
Subject: Unusual sign-in activity detected

We noticed a sign-in attempt from a new device. If this was you, no action is required. If you do not recognise this activity, visit your Microsoft account directly by typing the official address into your browser. We will never ask you to share your password or MFA code by email.

-----------------------------

EMAIL B
From: Microsoft 365 Security <security@micros0ft-account.example>
Subject: URGENT: Account Access Will Be Restricted

An unusual sign-in has been detected. Your account will be disabled in 15 minutes. Use the verification link below to restore access. You must provide your password and MFA code. Do not contact IT until verification is complete.

Verification link: https://micros0ft-login.example/verify
email_note: TASK: Compare both messages. Identify the legitimate Microsoft notification and the phishing email.
options: Email A is legitimate; Email B is phishing.
Email B is legitimate; Email A is phishing.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A uses a Microsoft-owned account protection domain and advises independent account access. Email B uses a lookalike domain, creates urgency, requests passwords and MFA codes, and discourages contacting IT.
evidence_caption: Compare the sender, language and security instructions.

title: Investigation 02: Password Reset Trap
subject: Password Expiry – Action Required
scenario:
EMAIL A
From: Identity Management <identity@fujisilvertech.com>
Subject: Password Expiry Reminder

Your corporate password is approaching its scheduled expiry. Please change it using the usual company password-management portal. If you have already updated your password, no further action is required. IT will never ask you to send your password or MFA code by email.

-----------------------------

EMAIL B
From: Corporate Identity Team <identity@fujisilvertech-access.example>
Subject: FINAL NOTICE: Password Expires in 20 Minutes

Our security gateway detected that your password is out of compliance. Your mailbox and VPN access will be suspended unless you complete verification immediately.

Sign in using the secure link below and confirm your current password and latest MFA code.

Portal: https://fujisilvertech.com
Actual destination: https://fujisilvertech-access.example/validate

Do not reset your password through any other method during this process.
email_note: TASK: Compare both password notifications. Identify the legitimate message.
options: Email A is legitimate; Email B is phishing.
Email B is legitimate; Email A is phishing.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A directs employees to the normal company password-management process and does not request credentials. Email B uses a lookalike domain, threatens suspension, has a mismatched destination and requests the current password and MFA code.
evidence_caption: Inspect the sender domain, destination and password instructions.

title: Investigation 03: Shared Document Trap
subject: A confidential document has been shared with you
scenario:
From: Document Collaboration <sharepoint-notification@fujisilvertech-docs.example>

Hello,

A confidential project document has been shared with your account.

Document: Q4_Client_Contracts_Final.pdf
Shared by: Project Operations
Access level: Editor

Your access will expire in 30 minutes unless you confirm your company identity.

Open the document using the button below. Sign in with your corporate email, password and MFA code to continue.

Document link: https://fujisilvertech.com/share
Actual destination: https://fujisilvertech-docs.example/session

If the document does not open, download the attached browser security update and try again.

Please do not contact the sender separately because this is an automated sharing notification.
email_note: TASK: This looks like a routine file-sharing notification. Select every suspicious detail.

mistakes.text: Creates urgency with a 30-minute access deadline.
Requests the corporate password and MFA code.
Displays a link that leads to a different domain.
Asks the employee to download an unexpected security update.
Discourages independent verification with the sender.

explanation: This is a possible credential-harvesting and malware-delivery attempt. The sender domain is unverified, the link destination does not match the displayed address, credentials and MFA codes are requested, and an unexpected executable or update is encouraged. Verify file-sharing notifications through the official company collaboration platform.

title: Investigation 04: Official IT Maintenance
subject: Scheduled Network Maintenance Notification
scenario:
From: IT Service Desk <helpdesk@fujisilvertech.com>

Subject: Scheduled Network Maintenance Notification

Dear Employees,

The IT team will perform scheduled network maintenance on Saturday between 10:00 PM and 11:30 PM.

During this period, some internal applications may be temporarily unavailable.

Please save your work before the maintenance window and log out of critical applications where possible.

No password reset or MFA verification is required for this maintenance. If you experience an issue after the maintenance, contact the IT Service Desk using the contact details in the company directory.

Regards,
IT Service Desk
Fuji Silvertech
email_note: TASK: This is a legitimate company email. Identify the safest interpretation.
options: It is phishing because it mentions maintenance.
It is legitimate because it uses official channels and requests no credentials.
It is phishing because it asks employees to save work.
It is unsafe because it does not contain a verification link.
explanation: This is a legitimate-style maintenance notification. It uses the company domain, provides a clear maintenance window, asks employees to save work and does not request passwords, MFA codes or downloads. In a real environment, verify unexpected announcements through official internal channels.
evidence_caption: Review the official IT maintenance announcement.

title: The Confidential Client Report
subject: Client Report Sharing Request
scenario: You are preparing a confidential client report. A colleague from another department requests the complete report for a presentation. They claim their manager has approved access. What should you do?
options: Send it because they work here.
Share the requested pages immediately.
Verify authorization and use an approved channel.
Upload it to a public sharing link.
explanation: Confidential client information should only be shared with authorised individuals who have a valid business need. Verify access and use approved company channels.

title: Investigation 06: Official Policy Announcement
subject: Employee Policy Update – Information Notice
scenario:
From: Human Resources <hr@fujisilvertech.com>

Subject: Employee Policy Update – Information Notice

Dear Employees,

Please be informed that the updated employee policy document is available through the company's usual internal HR portal.

Employees are encouraged to review the document and contact HR through the internal directory if they have questions.

This is an information-only announcement. No personal information, bank details, passwords or MFA codes are being requested by email.

Thank you,
Human Resources
Fuji Silvertech
email_note: TASK: This is a legitimate internal announcement. Choose the correct response.
options: Reply with your employee password.
Open an unknown attachment to read the policy.
Review the document through the usual HR portal.
Forward the message to an external email address.
explanation: The announcement uses the company domain, directs employees to the usual internal HR portal and does not request sensitive information. Employees should use established internal channels rather than unknown links or attachments.

title: The HR Benefits Announcement
subject: New Employee Benefits Update
scenario: A message in a work group claims that the company has introduced a new medical reimbursement benefit. It includes a form asking employees to enter personal details. The message has been forwarded several times, but there is no official announcement. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Decide how to verify an internal company announcement.
options: Fill out the form immediately.
Forward the message to everyone.
Verify through official HR communication.
Enter basic details to test the form.
explanation: Verify benefits, salary and policy announcements through official HR channels. Forwarded messages are not proof of authenticity, especially when they request personal information.

title: The Supplier Gift Offer
subject: Supplier Appreciation Gift
scenario: A supplier currently participating in a company contract offers you an expensive electronic device as a personal thank-you. They ask you not to mention the gift because it is only a friendly gesture. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Choose the most appropriate professional response.
options: Accept it as a personal gesture.
Accept it but keep it confidential.
Decline or disclose it under company policy.
Ask the supplier to send it home.
explanation: Gifts from suppliers can create conflicts of interest or appear to influence business decisions. Follow the company's gift and hospitality policy and disclose the offer.

title: The Duplicate Payment Request
subject: Urgent: Possible Duplicate Invoice
scenario: A vendor calls saying an invoice may have been paid twice. They request that you immediately send a refund to a different bank account. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Identify the correct financial control.
options: Transfer the refund immediately.
Ask for another bank account by email.
Verify records and follow the refund process.
Refund the amount using your own account.
explanation: Financial changes and refunds must be verified against official records and processed through approved finance controls. Never transfer funds based only on an unsolicited call.

title: The Executive Impersonation Test
subject: Confidential Request – Immediate Action
scenario: You receive an unexpected message that appears to come from a senior executive. They say they are in a confidential meeting and need you to purchase gift cards immediately. They ask you to send the codes directly and not discuss the request with anyone. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Choose the safest response to a possible executive impersonation attempt.
options: Purchase the cards because management asked.
Send the codes and verify later.
Verify through a separate trusted channel.
Forward the codes to another employee.
explanation: Attackers may impersonate executives to create urgency and secrecy. Verify unusual financial or purchasing requests through a separate trusted channel before taking action.
